mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that lead to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive more than 55% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive more than 60% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average signals strengthening consumer demand, which is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS > 12-month MA and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative more than 45% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to negative sentiment and lower S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive more than 55% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL is rising, and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive more than 55% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases sharply and UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases sharply and UNRATE decreases, and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive more than 60% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST > 6-month MA and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative more than 45% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in GDP (GDPC1) signals a strong economic expansion, which is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially in a late-cycle expansion regime.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 increases for 3 consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis fails.
